The 8 pairs the strong clause certifies are untraced against the interpreter.

## 51 The checker and the one library
- **Measured by the overloading judgement on private library copies** (`reviews/overloading-judgement.md`, its driver, variant scripts and captures under `reviews/overloading-judgement/`). The library's overload sets are repaired by its own devices: traits for the range kinds, marker traits plus `excludes` for the array `MIN`/`MAX` arms and `String`'s juxtaposition, the `StandardMinMax` `(T,T)` slip corrected (built, row 421), and names plus a `typecase` for `openRangeHelper`; measured on copies, `CAP` goes from 17 to 5, the 12 different-list errors going and the 5 left a same-list class the flattening removes, and `MIN`/`MAX`, juxtaposition and the slip go to 0 (the devices not yet built are batch 7b's rung L's, answer 9). For `fill`, declaring both forms where the array diamond meets, at `StandardMutableArrayType` and `ImmutableArray1` (the variant its script measured, though its text says the leaves; `compile-ladder/rung-tabulate/REPORT.md:190-194`), and giving the function form a second name clears every `fill` refusal and both factory refusals, the same as renaming the value form; that shape is built. Row 398 is re-attributed: the paper's return-type rule accepts the permuted override, and the failure is written static arguments handed by position to a different arm. Neither path has enforced the specification's sentence that overloads may not differ in static parameters since 2007. It is 2009 text that displaced the 1.0 release's own section on the subject.

## 75 The checker and the one library
- **The compiled checker reads a `comprises` clause as the 2012 texts do for a generic subtrait: it may extend the closed trait when the trait table knows at least one type that immediately extends it and each such type is below a listed type** (`compile-ladder/rung-comprises-checker/`; POSITIONS, "`AnyIntegral`'s closure and how the checker reads `comprises`"; rows 459, 487-490). The rule: `isEligibleToExtend` has a third disjunct, `(!tt.getArgs.isEmpty && everyKnownSubtypeListed(tt, comprises, analyzer))`, and the method beside it (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/TypeHierarchyChecker.scala:247-287`); the method is `reviews/anyintegral-comprises-ways/shadow-thc.py:52-64` byte for byte. The known types are the trait table's: the unit being checked and every api in its environment (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/TraitTable.scala:99-110`), compared by simple name. The specification states the rule ("The specification reads a `comprises` clause as the later Types chapter does" under "The specification and the repository's lineage"). Gated by `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/ComprisesGenericSubtrait.test`, which links and runs the library's shape in its own names (`AnyWhole comprises { SmallWhole, LargeWhole }` above the unlisted `Whole[\W extends Whole[\W\]\]`) and a listed extender of a generic subtrait, printing `PASS`. Still refused: a plain unlisted extender (`XXX10i`); a generic subtrait no known type extends, unless an unrelated trait of the same simple name in the environment has an extender below a listed type (row 490; `compile-ladder/rung-comprises-checker/probes/skeptic/name-collision.txt`); one that a known type below no listed type extends. For a generic closed trait the extender's self type is compared with the clause in the subtrait's own type-variable names, so the verdict depends on how the extender spells its type variable: `trait Both[\T\] extends { Full[\T\], Tag[\T, ZZ32\] }` is accepted over `Box[\T\] comprises { Full[\T\] }` and `Both[\S\]` refused (row 489, gated by `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXComprisesGenericRenamed.test`); the same capture accepts a false clause inside row 414's gap. A new section, "Declarations with Static Parameters" (`advanced/overloading.tex:531-651`), states the paper's three rules with the Return Type Rule over every instance, exclusion by the 2011 paper's existential reduction with instantiation exclusion (whether a bound that rules out the only static arguments at which two parameter types could meet makes them exclude each other is left open in "Passages not yet revised", the compiled checker taking that step for a named forced argument), the `GenPlainRTR` shape as "Not allowed" beside the paper's repair, and in a callout the positional rule as the compiled implementation's restriction for two declarations with as many static parameters of their own (the POPL recheck's item 1.3), and that neither implementation runs the paper's repair today (rows 159 and 537), with a reordering override as its example. Batch 7b's rung S writes it into the specification with a callout recording the Working Draft's `Object` (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/trait-parameters.tex:49-50`) and naming the compile path's `Object` setting (row 412) as the divergence until the switch-over.
== 43

The checker reads a `comprises` clause the 2012 way (the later Types chapter, `types.tick:384-389`, and Welterweight): a generic child of a closed trait is eligible when every type the checker knows under it is listed (`everyKnownSubtypeListed`), with an S1 callout in `Specification/basic/traits.tex`; the clause and walk stay as they are; a ledger row records the hole every way but the 2008 clause shares (a program's own `Integral` subtype in another component is not caught). Built. The api's overloading and return-type errors this let through are resolved by batch 7b (answer 9's families) and batch 8 (the meet rule and the residue).

The checker keeps the paper's three rules with two changes: the return-type rule is checked over every instance, and one narrow rule stays, that two generic arms in the more-specific relation agree on their static parameters position by position (Java's overriding rule; it closes row 398). Walk dispatches by declared domains, which ends its dependence on declaration order. The library's refused families are repaired by its own devices. No model line changes. Batch 7b, rungs S, C, W and L. The judgement's section 10 items (walk and an unused unknown size, `seq`'s device, Naden's instantiation) took the record's defaults, listed for his review.
== 45
- **Conversions never change which declaration runs.** A conversion is applied to make a call possible and never changes which declaration runs when one already fits; declarations are chosen by the coercion chapter's order, applicability and specificity taken on declared, quantified domains as answer 9 words them (a generic declaration fits when some instance within its bound fits); the chosen declaration is then instantiated by answer 8's promotion, its coercions inserted statically, and the rewritten call dispatches on the converted values; a numeral whose candidate types are incomparable reads as `ZZ32` (`ZZ64` or `ZZ` by magnitude), stated once in the inference chapter. So a generic arm over `T extends Number` beside a plain arm over `Any` runs the generic at `ZZ64` for a mixed-width call, the specialised instance; plain declarations are untouched; the broader rule (his own idea, "if there is a conversion to a specific type, it should be applied. And only if all combinations are exhausted and we haven't reached a specific implementation, then we go to a plain implementation") is not taken. His principle behind it: "we must make it fast, and generic is never fast. So make it fast." — fast code a JVM can specialise. With it, the inference rule: the checker infers a static argument with coercion, answer 8's promotion its number case, and keeps the expected type at a call written `f(x)` with a retry without it, so that a binding's coercion still applies; walk does the same at dispatch, re-instantiating the chosen declaration by the promotion from run-time types; the specification's type-inference chapter states it in the S1 form. == 49
- **Walk chooses coercions on the value, for now.** Walk has no static types, so it chooses a coercion on the value where the specification's coercion chapter and the compiled path resolve it statically (`Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:598-635`; `XXXCoercionStaticRungC`, `XXXCoercionStaticNarrowRungC`); accepted as the interpreter's limit, with one S1 callout at that passage in batch 7b's rung S; item 16 is closed with those two tests as its record. Walk is made to match after the switch-over, once the checker runs on interpreter programs and walk takes the static coercions the checker inserts. MicroGPT's static types are concrete, so the two paths agree on it.
== 50
- **The `comprises` passages read at the level of values (PLAN item 26, row 491).** The four passages of the specification that read a `comprises` clause at the level of types are restated at the level of values, "covers" is defined once, the Meet Rule gains the closed-trait case, and row 492 is repaired on both paths, in batch 7b's rungs S, C and W; the proof appendix keeps its existence lemmas and gives up static uniqueness for run-time uniqueness, a call whose argument's static type sits between typed by the intersection of its candidates' return types. The separate analysis session's proof addendum (`reviews/comprises-type-level-proof-addendum.md`, written at his request: he was "super scared that we are touching type theoretical things that I am totally unequipped to handle") has three points built into the briefs: Fortress already dispatches at run time with one static winner, so the performance cost claimed for such calls is unproven; the coverage search stays local to overload checking and does not widen assignment or ordinary subtyping; the proof holds only where closed families are closed, which row 487 leaves unenforced across some component boundaries. Its acceptance pair goes into rung C as written; the fallback (row 492's repair to batch 8) is used if the implementation needs broader subtype or closure repairs. One boundary for rung C's implementation review: the proof justifies the return-type intersection for ground declarations only, the more specific declarations that may run included; a generic declaration that needs a run-time instantiation must meet every static return promise at once, so the typing rule is not generalized on the proof, and the fallback is taken if the intended cases need the broader argument; a generic argument already instantiated, such as `G[ZZ32]`, stays in the ground case.
== 65
- **`NN32` coerces into `RR64`.** "if it fits, then there should be direct conversion. No question about it." — exact conversions are implicit, lossy ones explicit, answer 8's own criterion. One api line and one body line, a test, and the specification's callout on answer 8 reworded; in batch 8's library work, not in 7b's overloading rungs, since a new coercion changes which calls need one.
== 69
- **The team demos that write no static argument for a generic reduction** are respelled with their static arguments when a batch has a free slot (not before 7b), with a report-only demo stage; under the paper's instance rule the checker binds the bound instead of `Bottom` (row 425), so whether a demo runs unchanged is read again before the respelling. "Let's not touch them and we'll make them run later. If they will still need to be rewritten then ... then let's do it whenever."
== 86
- **The S1 form**, the layered form the team used for 1.0 and its 2009 draft: a labelled callout at each changed passage that prints in every build (not a `\note`); a revival section in Appendix I (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex`), each entry with the reason, the original sentences quoted with their path and line in the unrevised copy, and route C with what reversing to it would take; one paragraph in the front matter; the full reasoning in a repository document. The unrevised copy is called "the Working Draft of February 2011", in the team's own form, each citation giving the path and line in `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; Appendix I says once that the directory's name is misleading, since only `fortress.1.0.pdf` in it is the 1.0 release. Appendix I's introduction says that the entries follow the revival's decisions, route A the first of them, each naming its own (batch 7b's rung S).
== 88
- **Appendix I's small items.** `TotalComparison` extends `StandardMinMax[\TotalComparison\]` in the api and the component, its five restated members kept, so that it gets back `MIN` and `MAX` (row 461 closes; batch 7b's rung L; taken on the coordinator's recommendation, and he wants it explained in more detail when he has the energy, "I need to pay that down", so it is on the list for his review).
== 107
- **The phase-3 batches run on a standing go.** "I think you just carry on running the sequence of batches, I'll do the reset when I do it, If it stalls for a bit, I hope we'll recover without interruption. No need to complicate our runs with synchronization." And: "these are pre-approved. I want you to do autonomous overnight run." Each batch launches when the one before it has landed and its record is ready with no question open for him; a question a record raises goes to him first, except overnight, when it takes its recommended default and is listed for his review unless the default would reverse a decision of his, in which case that batch waits and the repair batch takes the slot; a run stalled by the limits is resumed with `resumeFromRunId`. A top-tier review in place of each coming batch record, in the form of `coordinator/climb-batch-7-review.md`, needs no further ask. The order is `PLAN.md`'s: batch 7b, then batch 8. "Go" starts background work only; a batch run needs his explicit go, which for phase 3 this standing go is.
== 108
- **The new batch practice, and what he expects of it.** The practice after the post-mortem of the batch practice: the synthesis of its two reviews and both archaeologies, written into the script, its manual and the protocol, the script reviewed, batch 7b's record rewritten to it and run on it, the landed batches' committed scratch cleaned in parallel; the post-mortem's four remaining questions (the output comparison, the review loops inside a batch, test names and messages, the cleaning's scope) take the synthesis's recommendations as defaults, listed for his review, unless a default would reverse a decision of his, in which case that part waits. "You can now redeem yourself by fixing this and, and, and showing me that you can be token efficient and not do bullshit jobs that you invented yourself." Every step spends the fewest workers the step needs and measures nothing the record already holds.
